front.title: Additional Methods for Generating Key Identifiers Values

abstract.t: This document specifies additional example methods for generating Key Identifier values for use in the AKI (Authority Key Identifier) and SKI (Subject Key Identifier) certificate extensions.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: defines the AKI (Authority Key Identifier) and SKI (Subject Key Identifier) certificate extensions. describes two example mechanisms for generating AKI and SKI values: a 160-bit SHA-1 (Secure Hash Algorithm) hash of the public key and a four-bit type field with the value 0100 followed by the least significant 60 bits of the SHA-1 hash. Both of these mechanisms were designed to not be critical to security. This document defines three additional mechanisms for generating Key Identifier values using SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512 that are similar to those examples defined in as well as one based on hashing the certificate's Subject Public Key Info field.

section.name: Additional Methods for Generating Key Identifiers
section.t: specifies two examples for generating key identifiers from public keys. Four additional mechanisms are as follows:

ol.li: The keyIdentifier is composed of the leftmost 160-bits of the SHA-256 hash of the value of the BIT STRING subjectPublicKey (excluding the tag, length, and number of unused bits).
The keyIdentifier is composed of the leftmost 160-bits of the SHA-384 hash of the value of the BIT STRING subjectPublicKey (excluding the tag, length, and number of unused bits).
The keyIdentifier is composed of the leftmost 160-bits of the SHA-512 hash of the value of the BIT STRING subjectPublicKey (excluding the tag, length, and number of unused bits).
The keyIdentifier is composed of the hash of the DER encoding of the SubjectPublicKeyInfo value.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: The security considerations of apply to certificates. The security considerations of apply to the hash algorithms.
While hash algorithms provide preimage resistance, second-preimage resistance, and collision resistance, none of these properties are needed for key identifiers.
